questions.q: A manager wants one report from the till system, an app and a spreadsheet. What is the first job to sort out?
options: Getting all that data into one place, which is what ingestion does
Choosing the colours for the charts
Cleaning and joining the data into a model
questions.explain: Ingestion is picking data up from its sources and landing it somewhere you can analyse it. Cleaning, joining and modelling come in the next stage.

questions.q: Say you copy only the rows that changed since last night, using an 'updated at' time. What can quietly go missing?
options: Rows that were really deleted, because a deleted row leaves no time to find
questions.explain: In the worked example, 50,000 deleted orders stay in the destination and nobody gets an error. A full copy or reading the change log catches them.

questions.q: A table is small, and a report that is an hour old is fine. Which method does the post suggest?
options: A full copy on a schedule
Picking up files in small groups
questions.explain: A small table can happily use a full copy forever. Save the fancier methods for when you need fresher data or the copy gets too slow or costly.

questions.q: The database keeps a change log, and a reader that nobody is using still holds on to it. What is the risk?
options: The log fills up the disk, and in the worst case the database stops
Every row is copied twice a night
questions.explain: Reading the change log catches every change, but it needs setup and someone watching disk space. An unneeded reader should be removed.

questions.q: A load fails halfway and is tried again. What must the retry never do?
options: Load the same rows a second time
questions.explain: A retry must not create duplicates. Big word, simple idea: running the same load twice should leave you with the same data as running it once.
